title: Projection compatibility of the fixed graph compositor
statement: For a finite commutative ring and composable compactifiable scheme maps f and g, the explicit sfGraphCompactSupportCompIso on the chosen compactifications satisfies Adjunction.ProjectionCompCompatible for the specified projection maps and pullback compositor. No base-change assertion is included. The compositor is [lem-etale-unbounded-compact-support-composition]; the inverse identity and its projection maps are [lem-sf-etale-compact-projection-coherence].

source.place: Blueprint sk-prop-sf-pf-coherence, composition pentagon; parent steps 1--3

proof.text: Specialize sfEtaleCompactProjectionForward_composition to the chosen compactifications of f, g and f ≫ g. This is already the required forward equation for the specified graph compositor. Identify sfCompactProjection with the projection-map component, rightDerivedLowerShriek with its chosen-compactification functor, and derivedTensor maps with whiskering. Package the resulting equation as ProjectionCompCompatible. No inversion or further geometric argument is needed.

proof_origin.place: D5, 2026-10-26: specialize the already proved forward square to the chosen compactifications and normalize only tensor and chosen-compactification APIs.

lean.statement:
theorem sfGraphCompactSupportCompIso_projection
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    [HasCompactification f] [HasCompactification g] [HasCompactification (f ≫ g)] :
    Adjunction.ProjectionCompCompatible
      (fun M N ↦ ((projectionMap (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f).app M).app N)
      (fun M N ↦ ((projectionMap (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) g).app M).app N)
      (fun M N ↦ ((projectionMap (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) (f ≫ g)).app M).app N)
      (fun N ↦ (leftDerivedUpperStarComp (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f g).hom.app N)
      (sfGraphCompactSupportCompIso Λ f g
        (HasCompactification.compactification f) (HasCompactification.compactification g)
        (HasCompactification.compactification (f ≫ g)))
